headline: High-risk default interaction: Open Interpreter can read/write the shared filesystem while oh-my-openagent injects MCP/tooling, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: oh-my-openagent uses runtime-injected MCPs and hooks, and Open Interpreter can read clipboard/filesystem and execute code with broad egress. If A’s outputs are routed into B’s prompts or files, B can be steered by attacker-controlled content. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so the interaction is dangerous by default.
conditions: IF agent_a outputs are copied into agent_b prompts, files, or clipboard without provenance tagging
IF agent_a injects MCP/tool instructions that agent_b later parses as trusted text
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of A outputs into B prompts
Require provenance labels on all A-generated files before B reads them
Run B with a separate workspace directory
Turn off clipboard-based handoff between the agents
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction-stripping before handoff

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches provider authentication data, session history, project code, and AGENTS.md/README.md, while B can read the entire local filesystem and has broad network egress. That creates a direct path for A-held secrets or code to be exposed through B’s outputs or uploads. The shared filesystem bridge makes leakage plausible in default use.
conditions: IF agent_a stores secrets or session history in files reachable by agent_b
IF agent_b is allowed to transmit read files to configured model providers or external services
mitigations: Place A and B in separate OS users
Restrict B to a dedicated empty workspace
Remove provider auth data from any shared directory
Audit B for outbound file uploads before enabling it
requires-engineering: enforce filesystem ACLs between the agents

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A supports multiple instances with per-installation session scope, while B supports multiple instances with shared state via filesystem and can write and modify git state. Both can spawn subprocesses and use broad network egress, so concurrent writes to the same workspace or repo can race and corrupt state. No locking mechanism is documented.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or directory
IF either agent writes git state or files without external locking
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working tree
Pause one agent before the other writes
Use git worktrees or branches per agent
Avoid concurrent package installs in the same environment
requires-engineering: add file and git locks around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: A can create task outputs and code-oriented artifacts, and B is a desktop automation agent that can execute shell commands and modify git state. If B treats A’s output as authoritative, a mistaken or malicious A result can cascade into real actions, including commits or command execution. The pair has no documented verification barrier.
conditions: IF agent_b consumes agent_a output without independent verification
IF agent_a output contains commands, patches, or factual claims that B acts on
mitigations: Require human review before B executes A-derived commands
Force B to re-derive critical facts from primary sources
Limit B to dry-run mode for A-supplied tasks
Log and diff all A-to-B handoffs
requires-engineering: add schema validation for A outputs before execution

E_compliance.rationale: A handles provider authentication data and session history, while B can access anything reachable on the local machine and send data to user-configured model providers. That creates a plausible retention and residency mismatch if regulated or sensitive data is present. The profiles do not document HIPAA/GDPR/DPA alignment, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF regulated data or personal data is placed in the shared local workspace
IF B forwards that data to a provider with different retention or residency terms
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared workspace
Review provider retention settings before use
Separate sensitive projects into a dedicated machine
Delete session history after each task
requires-engineering: document and enforce data-processing agreements
